notes: Good aggression on the remote that won the game; four repeated HQ runs through Congratulations! on turn 6 fed the Corp about 12 credits for little gain, and the Doomscroll facecheck at 1-3 credits with no breaker was loose.
Simple, efficient install-and-score pattern from one iced remote against a passive Runner; nothing notably wrong, though the remote was thin.

Early R&D pressure was fine, but then it sat at 0 credits for turns and later clicked for credits for seven straight turns up to 27 credits, never contesting the remote where the Corp scored its last two agendas.
Economy was starved most of the game and it spent several turns clicking for credits with a full hand while discarding; once the Ansel/Vertigo/Drafter remote was up, scoring through it was sound.
Steady R&D and remote pressure with sensible tag management; playing Maintenance Access just to jack out of Archives was a clumsy use of two clicks.

R&D stayed behind only a Wave (no ETR) all game while the Runner ran it every turn, and the Corp spent spare clicks and 10-18 credits clicking for credits instead of icing it; the first remote agenda went out behind one cheap barrier.
It won through R&D, but sat on tags and lost Telework Contract and Daeg to trashes, stayed broke most of the game, and facechecked a four-ice remote with 4 credits.
After the early steal it clicked for credits for most of the game, reaching 38 unspent credits and almost never running, while the Corp scored three remote agendas unchallenged.
It played Neurospike for no effect and clicked for credits while HQ, flooded with three Lotus Haze, sat behind a single Hafrun; the Runner took them on consecutive turns.
Good use of Urtica Cipher and Anemone net damage plus Bladderwort to grind out a flatline while scoring; it did a few idle credit clicks while rich early on.
Clean, fast economy and scoring tempo; it relied on a thin remote against a rich Runner, which worked only because the Runner never ran.
Good economy and a decisive four-run HQ turn to win; it lost several resources to tag trashes and wasted a run into a known Envelopment it could not break.
It spent itself to 0-1 credits trashing resources, installed Next Big Thing behind a lone Paywall the Runner could pay through, and never added ETR ice to R&D, which was the Runner's winning route.
It hoarded 30+ credits clicking for money over many turns and did not contest the remote while Fujii Asset Retrieval and the final Hybrid Release were installed and scored.

Mostly purposeful multi-server pressure that won, but it jacked out past Saisentan in front of a twice-advanced Fujii (scored next turn) and ignored a fresh remote install that became a scored Hybrid Release.
It installed Project Ingatan twice behind ice it could not afford to rez, so both were stolen, then left a third agenda in HQ behind only Tithe.
Sound R&D lock using a cheap Buzzsaw break that won the game; it often clicked for credits and made only one R&D run per turn when several were affordable.
It kept installing agendas into a remote behind one Diviner with almost no money and lost three that way, played Neurospike for nothing, and lost Fujii from a thinly iced HQ.

It won mostly because Ansel blocked HQ steals, but it sat at 0-3 credits for over ten turns holding Hedge Fund and Petty Cash, repeatedly installed naked Nico Campaigns that got trashed, and lost Architect Deployment Test from an unrezzable remote.
It clicked for credits nearly every turn up to 75 credits without installing a breaker or meaningfully running, letting the Corp score Kingmaking and three Remastered Editions unopposed.
